title: Investigating the Influence of Prompt and Response Languages on LLM Content Generation
abstract: arXiv:2608.26186v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This study examines how prompt and response language influence the behavior of large language models. Using five models, we evaluated answers to 68 non translation questions across four language conditions: English to English, English to Norwegian, Norwegian to Norwegian, and Norwegian to English. After removing refused items, the dataset contains 1348 responses. We measure length differences with Cohen d, semantic fidelity with LabSE cosine similarity, and cross lingual keyword overlap with both raw and soft Jaccard. Prompt language has a strong effect on response length. With English output, Norwegian prompts shorten responses by about thirty seven percent. With Norwegian output, English prompts shorten responses by about forty one percent. translated_title: 探究提示语言与响应语言对大型语言模型内容生成的影响
translated_abstract: 本研究考察了提示语言和响应语言如何影响大型语言模型的行为。我们使用五个模型，在四种语言条件下评估了对68个非翻译问题的回答：英语到英语、英语到挪威语、挪威语到挪威语以及挪威语到英语。在移除拒绝回答的项目后，数据集包含1348个响应。我们通过Cohen d测量长度差异，通过LabSE余弦相似度测量语义保真度，并使用原始和软Jaccard计算跨语言关键词重叠度。提示语言对响应长度有显著影响。在英语输出时，挪威语提示使响应缩短约37%。在挪威语输出时，英语提示使响应缩短约41%。最大的跨语言对比显示，词数减少但令牌数减少较少，这反映了分词器的差异。尽管长度存在差异，语义相似度仍然保持较高。
tldr: 本研究揭示提示语言和响应语言对LLM生成内容长度有显著影响，但语义保真度保持稳定，突出了分词器在跨语言生成中的关键作用。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that prompt and response languages significantly affect LLM-generated content length, while semantic fidelity remains stable, highlighting the key role of tokenizers in cross-lingual generation.
